p: Getting there first. Wandsworth Town station is on the line out of Waterloo, and Clapham Junction, one of the busiest stations in the country, is close by too, so it's easy to reach from across south and central London by train. If you're driving, London parking is never a given, so check the options near the centre before you leave rather than circling the one-way system.

Before your session, everyone climbing will need a participation form completing, with parents or guardians signing for under-18s. Do it online at home and you'll breeze through check-in. There's usually a minimum age for climbers and rules about supervising little ones, so glance at those when you book, especially if you're juggling a toddler and a ten-year-old.

On the day, give yourselves a couple of hours all in. Arrive early, get harnessed and briefed, then make the most of your climbing time. A light snack beforehand and a water bottle go a long way. Leave rings and watches at home and keep nails short.

Want somewhere to burn off the last of the energy? King George's Park runs alongside the River Wandle with play areas and plenty of space, and the Wandle Trail follows the river for a gentle walk or cycle. Battersea Power Station, now packed with shops and restaurants, is a short hop away if you fancy finishing the day somewhere a bit special.
